document.abstract: The current onboarding and offboarding processes for production crews involve a set of often inconsistent and manual activities, which are repetitive and inefficient, leading to various issues such as longer delays in bringing people on to a production project, inconsistent permission enforcement when a project is over, and higher overall cost.

authors.bio: Seth Levenson is the head of technology at Sanofi and a former ETC Adaptive Production Blockchain co-chair. Levenson has been involved in media and entertainment (M&E) for more than 30 years. After involvement in TV production at DIC Entertainment and as the Group Director for Information Technology at ABC Television Network, in 2001, Levenson started 3 legged dog, Inc., a consulting service for the M&E industry, and served as president until 2020. From October 2017 to August 2020, Levenson was the director of the Entertainment Technology Center, University of Southern California’s Adaptive Production project and brought thought leadership to cloud computing, blockchain and integration technologies. As of August 2020, he has been head of technology at Sanofi, a global life sciences company committed to improving access to healthcare and supporting the people they serve throughout the continuum of care, headquartered in Paris, France.
authors.name: Seth Levenson

authors.bio: Randy Zhang is a principal architect at Cisco Systems and ETC Adaptive Production Blockchain co-chair. Zhang is a well-recognized industry expert on networking and an author of two books, one of which is in its fourth printing and has been translated into a foreign language. He also published extensively in peer-reviewed journals and industry magazines and is a frequent speaker at industry conferences. Zhang is passionate about innovation and holds three U.S. patents. Additional details are available from https://www.linkedin.com/in/randyzhang/
authors.name: Randy Zhang

authors.bio: Anthony Anderson is a senior director, Film Security at Universal Pictures. Anderson is a 16-yr veteran of the security industry, working specifically in the Content Protection space for M&E. He began his career working in the Anti-Piracy Department at NBCUniversal in 2005 and for the past six years has been the head of the Film Security Program at Universal Filmed Entertainment. While at Universal, Anderson has contributed to multiple patents and whitepapers related to watermarking, DRM systems, cloud security and new technologies in the security industry. Anderson received a bachelors in information systems from California State University, Northridge, an MBA from Pepperdine University and a CISSP from ISC2.
authors.name: Anthony Anderson

authors.bio: Albhy Galuten is the founder and the CEO of Agora Media. He is an American technology executive, futurist, and Grammy Award-winning record producer, composer, musician, orchestrator, and conductor. He has multiple issued patents in the areas content distribution and resolution, customer care, user interface design, and media aggregation and optimization. As a record producer, he has produced 13 number 1 singles with songs and albums selling over 100,000,000 copies. He has been nominated for seven and won two Grammy Awards, a Dramalogue award, and a BMI award.
authors.name: Albhy Galuten

authors.bio: Jim Helman is a chief technology officer at MovieLabs, where he is working on advance technologies for the future of production, securely, in the cloud, with real-time iteration and visualization. There, he also led cross-industry initiatives including driving worldwide standards for high dynamic range video, built the Entertainment Identifier Registry (EIDR) and raised the bar on content protection. Additional details are available at https://www.linkedin.com/in/jimhelman/
authors.name: Jim Helman

authors.bio: Max Roessler is a consulting metadata architect and data strategist specializing in working with executives to maximize the value of their data assets by conducting complex in-depth analysis and transforming those insights into robust operations. Additional details are available at https://www.linkedin.com/in/maxroessler/
authors.name: Max Roessler

authors.bio: Joel Sloss is a senior program manager at Microsoft Azure. Sloss has built solutions for enterprise IT and security for more than 25 years. He originally joined Microsoft in 1997 after having served as a technical editor for Windows NT Magazine, where he authored more than 100 articles and product reviews and contributed to several books. While at Microsoft, Sloss has managed product lines ranging from BackOffice to ISA Server, mobile services, and—more recently—security and compliance initiatives in the Azure engineering team. Also, during this time, he wrote numerous white papers on topics such as data protection, network security, secure management, architecture fundamentals, and policies and processes. His focus now is on the Digital Media & Entertainment industry, its compliance objectives (such as security certifications), and privacy needs in the public cloud.
authors.name: Joel Sloss
